title: Add gradient-sliced latency probe and automated rollback controller
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce a gradient-sliced latency detector that slices traffic by light-weight hash segments and computes per-slice latency gradients; adds an automated rollback controller that gates canary traffic based on slice-weighted slope anomalies and a configurable rollback budget.
description:
Context and motivation:
Traffic and latency regressions can be subtle and localized to particular traffic shapes (e.g., long-sequence prompts, low-frequency endpoints). Existing canary detectors operate on coarse aggregate percentiles and often miss progressive degradations that first appear as steady slope changes across small cohorts. This PR introduces a 'gradient-sliced' approach: we split traffic into many lightweight slices, compute per-slice latency gradients over multiple window sizes, and then fuse slice-level signals into a traffic-weighted slope anomaly score that is robust to noisy outliers and transient bursts.

What this implements:
- A new probe module (perf_canary.probes.gradient_sliced) that maintains N hash slices per route and computes exponential-weighted linear regression slopes for each slice across short/medium/long windows.
- Slice-weighted fusion: weights slices by request-volume stability and SLO impact to produce a single slope anomaly score per-route.
- Adaptive threshold calibration: baseline drift is estimated using exponential percentile deciles per-slice; thresholds auto-scale with traffic so low-volume slices don't dominate.
- Synthetic microburst injection harness (optional) to exercise slope detectors in CI and on-demand smoke runs.
- Automated rollback controller that plugs into rollout orchestration: if slope anomaly score exceeds configurable severity and sustained_duration, the controller first throttles new canary traffic, then issues a rollback when budget/hysteresis rules are met. Controller exposes: holdoff, grace_period, rollback_budget, per-slice quarantine list.
- Metrics and tracing: new metrics (gc_latency_slope, gc_slice_violation_count, gc_fused_score) and distributed trace spans for degenerate slices to enable fast debugging in Console.
